ios.desc:
Block ads in Safari — including YouTube. Stop trackers and protect your privacy with advanced DNS filtering. Free to use. Trusted by millions.

BROWSE SAFARI WITHOUT DISTRACTION
Block banners, popups, autoplay videos, and intrusive ads in Safari — including YouTube — free and without limitations.
Clean up websites and stay focused on the content you actually came for.

BLOCK TRACKING. PROTECT YOUR PRIVACY
Stop hidden tracking scripts and digital fingerprints used by companies to track your activity.
Protect your privacy while browsing and prevent personal data collection.

FASTER LOADING. LESS DATA USAGE
Improve page loading speed by removing ads and heavy scripts.
Save mobile data and battery life when browsing, streaming, or using limited plans or roaming.

DNS PROTECTION BEYOND SAFARI
Encrypted DNS filtering blocks annoyances and unwanted requests system-wide — not just in Safari — and keeps your DNS queries private from ISPs, networks, and third parties watching your traffic. 
Secure your connection on public Wi-Fi. Use family-safe DNS to filter adult content on a child's device.

FREE TO USE — WITH PRO FEATURES
Free forever: Safari ad blocking + basic privacy protection. No account or registration required.
Pro unlocks: advanced YouTube blocking, app protection via DNS, custom rules + security filters.
7-day free trial — upgrade seamlessly right from your live stats dashboard.

SEE THE DEFENSES IN ACTION
Monitor blocked ads and trackers with built-in statistics.
View protection status and monitoring data in real time.

FULL CONTROL WITH CUSTOM SETTINGS
- Customize allowlists and blocklists
- Choose DNS servers
- Create user rules for filtering

POWERFUL FILTERING TECHNOLOGY
Advanced in-house filters and other popular filter lists.
Includes protection against malvertising, phishing, and suspicious content.

TRUSTED AND TRANSPARENT
17 years of experience in ad blocking.
Fully open source on GitHub — inspect every line of code. No "acceptable ads" programs, no compromises.

USE SAFARI THE WAY IT SHOULD BE
Cleaner pages, fewer distractions, and better privacy.
AdGuard for iOS gives you control over Safari browsing and DNS protection.

Privacy policy: https://adguard.com/privacy.html
Terms of use: https://adguard.com/eula.html
Follow us on X @AdGuard
Facebook: facebook.com/AdGuardEn/
Support: support@adguard.com

quotes.text:
Yes, AdGuard seems to do so and IIRC also has customizable block lists. The default includes Safari-only blocking but it is able to add a device-wide filter using Apple's API for VPNs. It seems to identify the various trackers used by the social media apps on my device, for instance.

App store link: https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id1047223162

GitHub link: https://github.com/AdguardTeam/AdguardForiOS

System-wide blocking: https://adguard.com/en/blog/how-to-configure-system-wide-blocking.html

quotes.text: Strange, the download from the app store (https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adguard-adblock-privacy/id1047223162) is 100 MB, but my install somehow crept up to ~400 (logs, maybe?) over a couple of years of use. I don't have it installed any more, but it's wild how much this varies across devices. What phone do you use? I use a 2016 SE, I wonder if there's a bug that's consume extra space on a device as old (and likely untested by AdGuard) as mine?

quotes.text:
https://apps.apple.com/app/apple-store/id1047223162

Use whatever you want re: iOS or Android, but there are plenty of ad blockers on iOS.

I know AdGuard[0] claims to have the ability of blocking YouTube ads in Safari, but I also believe it's behind an IAP. Alternatively, an Invidious instance[1] will play videos without ads. It doesn't work for music videos (thanks DRM!), and I believe you have to set the video quality to DASH in Invidious's settings for Safari to be able to play it. Not as convenient as YouTube, sure, but if you hate ads enough I think it's worth it.

[0] https://apps.apple.com/us/app/adguard-adblock-privacy/id1047223162

[1] https://redirect.invidious.io
